works.name: Edelmore Diary
works.hero: A cottage-core diary for a child — kept on your own machine.
works.personal_stake: Built for Iona, who wanted to keep an Anne Frank–style diary on her own terms — and for her sisters Ada and Isla.
works.short_description: A private web diary shaped like a book — it opens to today's page, turns its pages, takes dictation, and reads entries back aloud.
substantive_description: Adaptive tools are usually designed apologetically — accommodation as patch, accessibility as afterthought. Edelmore is built from the opposite direction, on Universal Design for Learning: the design itself accommodates without naming the accommodation. It opens to today's page and turns its pages; voice transcription handles the writing for hands that struggle with a keyboard, and it can read entries back aloud with each word highlighted as it is spoken. It runs on a parent's homelab, behind Tailscale and the home LAN, and nobody reads it but the person who wrote it. The deeper argument is that scale-of-one design is a legitimate target: a tool built for one specific thirteen-year-old, in the shape of a book she imagined, is not a small project but a complete one at the scale it was meant for — what one tool, made for one person, looks like when it counts.

SvelteKit (TypeScript, Svelte 5 runes), SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind v4, StPageFlip, and argon2id, with optional WhisperX transcription and Kokoro TTS read-aloud; deployed with Docker and Caddy.

state.last: shipped and live at edelmore.sageframe.net; ho sequence through ho-11 (page-turn rewrite, View Transitions) closed; ho-12 (content single-source, anchored voice) and ho-13 (whole-entry narration) are open.
state.next: close ho-12 (content single-source / anchored voice), then ho-13 (whole-entry narration).
